_doc: T032 LEGAL gov-oracle (TT-478 / ICP-0002 / TT-658). Each case asserts the Catala-computed reduced-rate IHT charge equals the AUTHORITATIVE HMRC figure cited inline. oracle_verify.py runs the scope with `inputs` and requires the Computed-arm money to equal `expected_money_gbp`; a wrong rule literal turns the harness RED. Legal model (IHTA 1984 Sch 1A, single general component, NRB-only baseline, NO RNRB): baseline = estate_value - available NRB (IHTM45009 Step 2 deducts the NRB and is 'not increased by any RNRB'); donated amount = charitable_gift_amount (Sch1A Para 4); 36% applies iff donated >= 10% of baseline ('at least', IHTM45002 / Sch1A Para 2(2)); the charitable gift is IHT-exempt (s.23) so taxable = estate_value - charitable_gift_amount - NRB, then x rate. Figures live-sourced from gov.uk / the HMRC IHT Manual on `sourced_at` and must be re-verified against the live pages if edited (HALT fork 2: never assert a tax figure from memory).
statute: IHTA 1984 Schedule 1A (reduced rate of tax where 10% of net estate left to charity: Para 2(2) charitable-giving condition, Para 4 donated amount, Para 5 baseline amount); s.7 + Sch 1 (rates); s.23 (charity exemption)
synthetic_cases_note: Cases marked "synthetic": true are mechanical boundary probes for TT-863's mutation-adequacy harness, not published HMRC/gov.uk worked examples — their expected figures are derived directly from the rule's own statutory formula (same IHTA 1984 Sch 1A basis as the other 4 cases) and confirmed by running the real clerk/catala toolchain, never asserted from memory.

cases.label: above-10pct-36
cases.citation_quote: The estate can pay Inheritance Tax at a reduced rate of 36% on some assets if you leave 10% or more of the 'net value' to charity in your will.

cases.label: below-10pct-40
cases.citation_quote: The standard Inheritance Tax rate is 40%. It's only charged on the part of your estate that's above the threshold.

cases.label: exactly-10pct-boundary-36
cases.citation_quote: In order to qualify for the lower rate; the donated amount must be at least 10% of the baseline amount.
cases.note: donated 67,500 == 10% of baseline (675,000) -> qualifies ('at least' = >=). taxable = 1,000,000 - 67,500 - 325,000 = 607,500; x 36% = 218,700. Boundary case pins the >= (not >) comparator.

cases.label: no-charity-40-unchanged
cases.citation_quote: Your estate is worth £500,000 and your tax-free threshold is £325,000. The Inheritance Tax charged will be 40% of £175,000 (£500,000 minus £325,000).
cases.note: zero-charity path stays 40% and matches the existing IHT worked example (£70,000): taxable = 500,000 - 0 - 325,000 = 175,000; x 40% = 70,000 — proves no verdict flip vs IhtDeathCharge for the no-charity case.

cases.label: below-nrb-boundary-probe
cases.note: TT-863 mutation-adequacy boundary probe (NOT a cited HMRC worked example — see synthetic_cases_note). estate_value < NRB: both floor guards fire (baseline=$0, taxable=$0), so tax=$0 regardless of rate. Closes the taxable-else-literal-flip mutant (taxable's else-$0 -> $1 would make tax=$1*rate != $0). Empirically verified against the real clerk/catala toolchain during design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-11-tt-863-catala-mutation-adequacy-engine-design.md §7a).

cases.label: above-nrb-by-one-pound-boundary-probe
cases.note: TT-863 mutation-adequacy boundary probe (NOT a cited HMRC worked example). estate_value is exactly £1 above the NRB — the only whole-pound value that distinguishes a '> $0' guard from a '> $1' mutant (the harness's flip is always +£1). baseline=taxable=$1 (both guards true, then-branch), meets_ten_percent = (0 >= 0.10) = false -> rate=40%, tax = $1*0.40 = $0.40. Closes the baseline-comparator-flip and taxable-comparator-flip mutants (either flip switches the guard to false, dropping the affected value to $0, changing the final tax). Empirically verified against the real clerk/catala toolchain during design (§7a).
